Kumāradāsa
poet of Ceylon; later than Bhāravi an. earlier than Māgha who was influenced by Ku. Legends make him a contemporary of Kālidāsa; a late Ceylonese tradition identifies him with King Kumāra Dhātusena or Kumāradāsa (
-26 A. D.), son of Maudgalāyana; but according to the Madras ms. of his Jānakīharaṇa (

), he was the son of Mānita, who was military official of King Kumāramaṇi an. who died on the battle-field on the [Page205-b] day the child was born; an. a. a. invalid child, he was brought up by his maternal uncles Megha an. Agrabodhi. In Kāvyamīmāṁsā (p. 12, GOS. edn.), Rājaśekhara refers to Kumāradāsa a. being born blind; a verse of Rājaśekhara mentions Kumāradāsa a. a. of Jānakīharaṇa (see Smv. p. 45).

XX (1888). p.. 148-9; Bendall, ibid. p. 440; Nandargikar, Intro. to his 3rd edn. of Raghuvaṁśa (1897), p.. 121-7; I. E. Senaviratne, Life of Kālidāsa, Colombo, 1901. On Ku. an. Vāmana, see JRAS. (1901) p. 266; but the basis of this discussion is wrong a. the real reading of the concerned verse in J. haraṇa is different.
